mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tiny home on wheels and one with a permanent foundation?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main difference lies in mobility and classification. A tiny home on wheels, often referred to as a Tiny House on Wheels (THOW), is typically built to RVIA standards and designed to be movable. It's often classified as a recreational vehicle or park model, impacting where it can be legally parked. A tiny home with a permanent foundation is affixed to land, similar to a traditional house. These are usually classified as Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) or single-family homes and must comply with local building codes. Each type has distinct permitting, zoning, and utility connection requirements.
acceptedAnswer.description: A tiny home on wheels is mobile and often classified as an RV, while one with a permanent foundation is fixed to land, classified as an ADU or home, and subject to traditional building codes.
